subject: PoC trial plan - deployment mode & success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Garcia <laura.g@acme-corp.com>, Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: PoC trial plan - deployment mode & success criteria

Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the PoC scoped and on the calendar.

Recap of needs from our conversation:
- Primary concern: low-latency inference for customer-facing product with predictable throughput peaks (expected steady-state ~60 req/s, peaks ~120 req/s).
- Data residency & auditability requirements for PII in EU / US (we discussed options).
- Security: SOC 2, SSO, and audit logs are must-haves for procurement.

Key question: For the PoC, which deployment mode should we target? Options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest to start), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput), or Private (VPC/on-prem for strict data isolation). My recommendation for this workload is Dedicated capacity for the PoC so we can hit throughput SLOs and test autoscaling and observability. If you prefer, we can spin up a Hosted API trial first then move to Dedicated — both are viable.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (attached: acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf):
1) Kickoff & environment setup (week 0): provisioning Dedicated capacity, account & SSO setup, network peering (if applicable).
2) Baseline tests (week 1): replay sample traffic, validate latency & throughput under expected sequences.
3) Integration + end-to-end testing (week 2): app integration, logging, tracing, and metric collection.
4) Acceptance & handover (week 3): run acceptance tests against success criteria below, review results.

Success criteria (we should confirm these with you):
- 95th percentile latency < 400ms for production-sized prompts under steady throughput
- Capability to sustain 120 req/s for 15+ minutes without degradation
- Logs/audit capture for all requests and KMS-managed keys for any secrets
- Clear ownership sign-off from Tom (CTO) and Priya (Infra lead)

Can you confirm:
- Preferred deployment mode for the PoC?
- Any additional success criteria we should add?
- Target kickoff week (we have availability the week of May 3).

Next steps from our side if you confirm Dedicated: I’ll loop in our solutions engineer (Jordan) to scope the infra changes, draft a short SOW, and spin up a dev Dedicated cluster for testing.

Thanks — looking forward to locking dates.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC trial plan - deployment mode & success criteria

Ben —

Thanks for the great recap and the attached plan. Quick answers from our side:

Deployment mode: We’d prefer to target Dedicated capacity for the PoC. Primary reasons:
- Predictable performance for customer-facing latency SLAs
- Data residency controls and easier compliance mapping
- We expect to need GPU isolation for the model sizes we’ll test

Success criteria (please add these to the document):
- 95th percentile latency < 350ms under steady-state 60 req/s (we can be stricter than the initial ask)
- Ability to sustain 120 req/s for 15 minutes with p95 < 500ms
- End-to-end error rate < 0.1% over a 24-hour test window
- Full request/response logging to our SIEM (we’ll share details)
- SSO integration (we use Okta) and KMS for key management

Stakeholders / approvers:
- Tom Evans (CTO) — tom.evans@acme-corp.com
- Priya Singh (Infra lead) — priya.singh@acme-corp.com
- Laura Garcia (Product) — laura.g@acme-corp.com

Timeline: We are aiming to kick off the PoC the week of May 3. Procurement timeline: ~2-3 weeks for PO/contract sign-off on our side (we’ll start immediately).

Procurement asks: Can you provide a short SOW + ballpark pricing for a 4-week PoC on Dedicated capacity so our procurement team has something to review? Also please highlight any data transfer or egress costs we should be aware of.

Thanks —
Laura
Product Lead, Acme Corp

Laura / Tom —

Great — thanks for confirming Dedicated and for tightening the latency targets. We’ll incorporate the stricter p95 into the acceptance tests.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Jordan (cc’d) will scope the Dedicated cluster size (GPU type, pool sizing) and provide a perf baseline doc by Monday.
- I’ll draft a short SOW and ballpark pricing for a 4-week PoC (deliverable, timeline, responsibilities, exit criteria). Expect a doc and approximate numbers by EOD Monday.
- We’ll include notes on egress and any potential transfer costs; for most hosted + dedicated flows we can estimate based on expected payload sizes.

Proposed kickoff: week of May 3 (we’ll plan a 60-minute kickoff to align infra/networking and access). Please confirm preferred day/time that week and I’ll send a calendar invite.

A couple of clarifying questions for procurement and infra teams on your side:
1) Do you require a network peering/VPN for Dedicated, or can we use secure public endpoints with VPC firewall rules?
2) For SIEM integration — which log format / endpoint should we plan to push to? (Tom / Priya, can you advise?)

Attachments: redwood_poc_statement_of_work.docx (SOW draft)

If ok, I’ll also open a HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign for a short PoC addendum to speed the procurement path (link will be included in my next note).

Best,
Ben
